parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the oscillations of a pendulum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Carry out the following instructions, referring to Figs. 4.1 and 4.2. The pendulum has already been set up for you. Fig. 4.1 Fig. 4.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure, and record in the first row of Table 4.1, the height h of the pendulum bob above the bench.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Pull the pendulum bob a small distance to one side, as shown in Fig. 4.2, and release it. It will oscillate backwards and forwards between A and B , as shown in Fig. 4.2. One complete oscillation is from A to B and back to A . Measure the time t for 10 complete oscillations. Record this value in the table. Table 4.1 h / cm t / s T / s T 2 / s 2

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Without changing the height of the clamp, adjust the string to shorten the pendulum by approximately 10 cm. Repeat steps (a)(i) and (a)(ii) .

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Repeat step (a)(iii) to obtain 3 more sets of readings. [2]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) For each value of height h , calculate the time T for one complete oscillation using the equation T = t –– 10 . Record these values in the table.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the values of T 2 and record these in the table. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of T 2 / s 2 ( y -axis) against h / cm ( x -axis). [4]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ........................................[2]
